canonical_data: append-only conversation streams of messages, tool calls, results, compactions, and recovery facts; accepted submissions with their claims and leases; and per-conversation persistent state, held in memory, SQLite, an adapter database, or Cloudflare Durable Object storage
current_repo_note: The root LICENSE is the full Apache-2.0 text and every packages/*/package.json manifest declares Apache-2.0. The runtime depends on the MIT-licensed Pi agent core and model API packages, which the Atlas reviews as the separate Pi record.
strengths: A documented accepted-work contract: every admitted submission is recorded before model work begins and reaches one durable outcome, with crash recovery, bounded retries, durable tool steps, and resumable delegated tasks

The sandbox is a declared, swappable boundary: an in-memory virtual shell, the host with an allowlisted environment, or provider sandboxes such as Daytona, E2B, Modal, Vercel, and Cloudflare through thin adapters

Open at each layer: Pi's provider catalog plus custom OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoints, MCP connections, database adapters, OpenTelemetry, Sentry, and Braintrust export, verified channel events, and Node.js, Cloudflare, and CI deploy targets
weaknesses: Young and fast-moving: first published in 2026, and the 2.0 release of 2026-07-31 was a breaking redesign that removed workflows and reset persisted state
There is no built-in approval or pause-for-human primitive; operator control is assembled from state-gated tool mounting, MCP annotation hints, aborts, and timeouts in application code
The local sandbox gives the model a real host shell with no isolation by design, and most provider sandboxes cannot stop a cancelled command that is already running
why_it_matters: Flue packages the coding-agent harness shape — a model loop with file and shell tools, skills, subagents, and a workspace — as a deployable TypeScript framework, and pairs it with an unusually explicit durability contract rather than leaving recovery to the integrator.
